hyps.why: Adding a conv on a missing direct input-to-output edge restores a major path (up to +78 points), whereas replacing an existing op gives small or negative changes.
Replacing a skip with a conv on the direct edge hurt on all three datasets, since the skip already gives a useful shortcut path.
Swapping an existing pool for a conv on the direct edge gives roughly zero or negative changes, unlike filling an empty edge.
Adding a skip where the direct edge was missing restores a gradient and feature path and gains more than replacing an existing conv.
When edge 3 is absent, the output relies on edges 4 and 5, so a skip on edge 5 helps much more (+14 on ImageNet16) than usual.
With edges 3 and 4 missing, replacing the skip on edge 5 with a conv lost 3.6 to 14 points, the reverse of the skip gain.
Removing edge 0 hurts far more (-3.4 to -6.8) when the direct input-to-output edge is already missing, since fewer input paths remain.
Replacing a parameter-free pool with a conv gains on all three datasets (+1.4, +1.1, +4.4), with a huge gain in the all-pool parent.
Replacing a conv with a skip on the direct edge gives a modest gain, smaller than filling the empty edge with a skip.
In a parent whose other edges are all skips, adding a conv on edge 0 gives a huge gain (+43 on CIFAR-10), because the cell otherwise has almost no learnable transformation.
